_: PIN — the ROSTERS of the two largest test populations, by NAME (F1).
why_a_manifest_and_not_a_count: Every N/N this mission cites is a ratio whose denominator is DISCOVERED FROM
THE ARTIFACT BEING GRADED. verify-all.sh globs `find src -name '*.test.mjs'`
and cargo discovers its own #[test] functions, so a deleted test does not
lower the numerator — it LEAVES THE POPULATION, and the denominator follows
it down.
MEASURED, not argued. In a disposable worktree off 56af276, delete one
globbed test file (web/src/ui/statsPanel.test.mjs) and one named Rust test
(zone::tests::capacity_rules — one of only two guards on capacity_from_area):
bash scripts/verify-all.sh   ->  VERIFY OK — 53/53 steps green
cargo test -p ds-core        ->  test result: ok. 199 passed; 0 failed
node scripts/gates/reconcile.mjs -> reconcile OK (exit 0)
Fully green, and NOTHING NAMED THE LOSS. That is verbatim the R8 defect
verify-all.sh's own header documents, fixed for the skip() path only; the
glob path and cargo's own discovery were never covered.
The instrument that could have caught it already computed the number and
threw it away: reconcile's asserting-file census printed `83 file(s) … 43
globbed by a runner` before the deletion and `82 … 42` after, and still
exited `reconcile OK`. The count was PRINTED, never ASSERTED.
CLAUDE.md:198 has stated the rule the whole time and nothing enforced it:
Rust tests are 'counted BY NAME, because a matching number with a missing
name is a regression.' This file is that manifest.
contract: STRICT SET EQUALITY, both directions, as TWO separate checks.
A member in this pin but not on disk is RED — a test was deleted or
renamed, and coverage left silently. This is the F1 direction.
A member on disk but not in this pin is RED — a test arrived unexamined,
and its name has never been read by anyone re-pinning deliberately.
Two checks and not one equality, for the reason SG5 gives: a single
'the roster moved' would make the reader do the diff, which is exactly what
a count did. A rename must read as one GONE and one NEW, never as net zero.
The count is deliberately NOT re-asserted anywhere. Equal named sets have
equal sizes, so a count check beside this equality is a tautology (R16),
and a tautology on a board is worse than nothing: it looks like coverage.

js: The on-disk side is NOT re-implemented here. reconcile.mjs extracts the
shell pipeline out of verify-all.sh's own source and RUNS it. So the roster
is reconciled against what the runner will actually execute, not against a
second walker that can drift from it. Change the glob and the derivation
changes with it; delete the pipeline and the extraction fails RED rather
The extraction is anchored to the WHOLE CONSTRUCT — `while IFS= read -r t;
do run "…" node "$t"; done < <( … )` — and not to the pipeline alone,
because a glob that no longer feeds a loop that RUNS each file is a list,
not a population. Exactly one such loop is expected: zero means the anchor
is gone, two means the runner grew a second globbed population this pin
rust: `cargo test -p ds-core -- --list`, parsed for `<name>: test` lines. Names,
never a count — and the parse is cross-checked against cargo's OWN
`N tests, M benchmarks` summary line, so a regex that silently stops
matching cannot masquerade as a shrinking population.
reconcile also asserts verify-all.sh still invokes `cargo test -p ds-core`,
anchored to the `run "…" cargo test -p ds-core` LINE and not to the string
anywhere in the file. A roster reconciled against a suite no runner runs is
a pin on a population that grades nothing.
That anchoring is not decoration — it is a defect the sabotage round found
in this very guard. The first version matched the string anywhere; sabotage
E2 replaced the `run` line with a `skip` and left the two COMMENT mentions
of the same command, and reconcile returned `reconcile OK`, exit 0, with
nothing running the Rust suite. Same family as export-parity's code-path
specificity axis, found by breaking the mechanism rather than by review.

update_discipline: --why is REQUIRED; a bare --update-roster is REFUSED. This is the precedent
already in the tree (scripts/drawing-set.test.mjs, whose --update refuses
without --why for the same reason): a manifest anyone can regenerate on a
whim is a count with extra steps.
The attribution is stamped PER MEMBER, onto the members that actually moved,
and only those — the shape drawing-set.baseline.json uses for its per-sheet
`why`. Members already in the pin keep the reason they were pinned with; a
re-record cannot launder an old member's provenance by restating a new one.
An --update-roster with no difference is REFUSED too. A no-op re-record that
rewrites `updates[]` is how a provenance log becomes decoration.
Every run is appended to `updates[]` with its added and removed members named
in full. A removal recorded there is a deliberate retirement; a removal that
never appears there is the F1 defect.
